models.title: Singer-Terhaar fully-integrated risk premium component
models.summary: Risk premium under full global integration: asset–market correlation times asset volatility times the global market Sharpe ratio.

relationship.original_equation: RPiG = βi,GM RPGM = ρi,GM σi (RPGM / σGM)
relationship.locator: PDF: LM2 Forecasting Equity Returns, printed p. 88 (PDF p. 98), Eq. 4; applied printed p. 89 (PDF p. 99)
relationship.translation_notes: Curated form is the rightmost equality of Eq. 4, using the global Sharpe ratio SRgm = RPGM/σGM directly as an input. Decimal form (unit 1). The middle beta form is an equivalent restatement, not a separate record. Dimensional check: dimensionless × dimensionless × dimensionless = dimensionless premium.

variables.definition: Correlation of asset i with the global market portfolio
variables.context: same asset and global market portfolio as RPiG

variables.definition: Volatility of asset i, in decimal form
variables.context: same asset and horizon as RPiG

variables.definition: Global market Sharpe ratio: global risk premium per unit of global market risk, in decimal form
variables.context: same global market portfolio and horizon as RPiG

variables.definition: Risk premium for asset i under full global integration, in decimal form
variables.context: same asset and global market portfolio as inputs

assumptions: Full integration: a single global market portfolio prices every asset via the CAPM.
Source assumption: pragmatic implementation sets compensation for non-diversifiable risk equal in every market (all Sharpe ratios equal the global one).
limitations: Fully-integrated component only; partial integration requires the blend record from batch b02.
Correlation and volatilities are estimated inputs with sampling error not modeled here.

sources.title: CFA Program Curriculum 2025 Level III Core Volume 1 — Asset Allocation
sources.locator: LM2 Forecasting Equity Returns, printed pp. 88–89 (PDF pp. 98–99), Eq. 4 and worked example
sources.evidence: Passage derives the integrated component as beta times the global premium, rewritten as correlation times asset volatility times the global Sharpe ratio, then applies it (German shares 0.70 × 17% × 0.30 = 3.57%).

sources.title: Equity Forecasting Models (AnalystPrep CFA Level III study notes)
sources.locator: Singer and Terhaar Analysis equation: integration term σi × ρ × ERPm/σm
sources.evidence: Page gives the integrated term as degree of integration times asset volatility times correlation times market premium over market volatility — the same correlation-volatility-Sharpe structure as the PDF's Eq. 4.
sources.redistribution: Short original paraphrase and single-formula transcription only; no extended quotation

references.method: Source inputs in decimals: 0.70 × 0.17 × 0.30 = 0.0357, matching published 3.57%.
references.provenance: Published result: LM2 worked example, printed p. 89 (PDF p. 99)

references.method: Source inputs in decimals: 0.50 × 0.07 × 0.30 = 0.0105, matching published 1.05%.
references.provenance: Published result: LM2 worked example, printed p. 89 (PDF p. 99)

rejection_cases.reason: Global Sharpe ratio is a required input; correlation and volatility alone cannot price the integrated premium.

models.inverse_notes: rho = RPiG/(sigi·SRgm) requires sigi·SRgm ≠ 0; sigi = RPiG/(rho·SRgm) requires rho·SRgm ≠ 0; SRgm = RPiG/(rho·sigi) requires rho·sigi ≠ 0. Zero correlation gives zero integrated premium (full diversification). Algebraic only; correlation is estimated, not caused, by inversion.

gaps: Quantity meanings asset_global_market_correlation, asset_return_volatility, global_market_sharpe_ratio, integrated_market_risk_premium are not in the runtime vocabulary snapshot and require extension.
Feeds the b02 blend record as the RPiG input; beta form (Eq. 3, batch b02) is an equivalent restatement.

models.title: Singer-Terhaar fully-segmented risk premium component
models.summary: Risk premium under complete segmentation: asset volatility times the segmented-market Sharpe ratio (asset as its own market portfolio).

relationship.locator: PDF: LM2 Forecasting Equity Returns, printed p. 88 (PDF p. 98), Eq. 5; applied printed p. 89 (PDF p. 99)
relationship.translation_notes: Curated form is the informative second equality of Eq. 5 (the first is an identity conveying no information, per the source). Decimal form (unit 1). Dimensional check: dimensionless × dimensionless = dimensionless premium.

variables.definition: Volatility (risk) of asset i, in decimal form
variables.context: same segmented asset market and horizon as RPiS

variables.definition: Sharpe ratio (compensation per unit of risk) in the segmented market, in decimal form
variables.context: same segmented asset market and horizon as RPiS

variables.definition: Risk premium for asset i under complete segmentation, in decimal form
variables.context: same segmented asset market and horizon as inputs

assumptions: Complete segmentation: each asset class in each country is priced in isolation (β = ρ = 1 with itself).
The segmented Sharpe ratio is supplied by analyst judgment (source example uses 0.35 for German shares, 0.25 for German bonds).
limitations: Fully-segmented component only; partial integration requires the blend record from batch b02.
Under segmentation the required premium could in principle be any value (per source); the volatility-times-Sharpe split is a framing, not a measurement.

models.title: Pension surplus as market value of assets minus present value of liabilities
models.summary: Surplus (funded status amount) equals the market value of assets minus the present value of liabilities at the stated discount rate.

relationship.locator: PDF: LM4 Surplus Optimization, printed p. 239 (PDF p. 249)
relationship.translation_notes: Both inputs are money levels at the same valuation date in the same currency; source works in USD billions. Negative surplus is underfunding. Dimensional check: currency − currency = currency.

variables.definition: Market value of the assets available against the liabilities at the valuation date
variables.context: same plan and valuation date as S

variables.definition: Present value of liability cash flows at the stated discount rate and valuation date
variables.context: same plan, valuation date, and discount rate as S

variables.definition: Surplus (funded status amount): positive when overfunded, negative when underfunded
variables.context: same plan, valuation date, and discount rate as inputs
variables.domain: Finite surplus; zero is exactly fully funded

assumptions: Assets and liabilities are valued at the same date; liabilities use the stated discount rate assumption.
Source assumption: liability discount rates follow regulation/tradition and are highly assumption-dependent.
limitations: Highly sensitive to the discount rate (source: 4% gives +0.239bn, 2% gives −0.539bn for LOWTECH); the rate choice is outside this definitional record.
Money-amount form; the companion funding-ratio record gives the percentage form.

sources.title: What should an overfunded corporate pension plan do with its surplus assets? (Milliman insight)
sources.locator: Milliman 100 PFI figures: $1.296tn assets against $1.156tn projected benefit obligations = $139bn funded-status surplus
sources.evidence: Article computes the funded-status surplus as plan assets minus projected benefit obligations (1.296 − 1.156 = 0.139 trillion), confirming the same assets-minus-liabilities definition.
sources.redistribution: Short original paraphrase and single-formula transcription only; no extended quotation

references.method: Source's USD-billion inputs: 2.500 − 2.261 = 0.239, matching published US$0.239bn at the 4% discount rate.
references.provenance: Published result: LM4 LOWTECH example, printed p. 239 (PDF p. 249)

references.method: At the 2% discount rate the source reports surplus −US$0.539bn on US$2.5bn assets, implying PVL 3.039bn; 2.5 − 3.039 = −0.539. Tolerance covers the source's rounded liability value.
references.provenance: Published result: LM4 LOWTECH example at 2% discount rate, printed p. 239 (PDF p. 249)

rejection_cases.reason: Present value of liabilities is required; assets alone cannot determine funded status.

models.inverse_notes: MV = S + PVL; PVL = MV − S. No singularities. Substitution check: S=0.239 with PVL=2.261 recovers MV=2.500. Algebraic only; the economically substantive inverse (choice of discount rate) is outside this record.

gaps: Quantity meanings pension_asset_market_value, pension_liability_present_value, pension_surplus are not in the runtime vocabulary snapshot and require extension.
Companion funding-ratio record in this batch gives the ratio form over the same inputs.

models.title: Pension funding ratio as market value of assets over present value of liabilities
models.summary: Funding ratio equals the market value of assets divided by the present value of liabilities; 1 is fully funded.

relationship.original_equation: Funding ratio = Market value (assets) / Present value (liabilities)
relationship.locator: PDF: LM4 Surplus Optimization, printed p. 239 (PDF p. 249)
relationship.translation_notes: Pure ratio of two money levels in the same currency; result is dimensionless (unit 1). Fully funded at 1, overfunded above 1, underfunded below 1, per source. Dimensional check: currency/currency = dimensionless.

variables.definition: Market value of the assets available against the liabilities at the valuation date (same definition as surplus record)
variables.context: same plan and valuation date as FR

variables.definition: Present value of liability cash flows at the stated discount rate and valuation date (same definition as surplus record)
variables.context: same plan, valuation date, and discount rate as FR

variables.definition: Funding ratio: 1 fully funded, above 1 overfunded, below 1 underfunded
variables.context: same plan, valuation date, and discount rate as inputs

assumptions: Assets and liabilities valued at the same date with the stated discount rate, same basis as the surplus record.
limitations: Ratio form suppresses the money scale of over/underfunding; pair with the surplus record for absolute amounts.
Discount-rate sensitivity is inherited from the liability present value and is outside this definitional record.
